c1.note: FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-10) lists 'Marketing solution providers, such as Mailchimp and Braze' among main competitors.

c2.note: 10-K lists 'Large, consolidated marketing automation software providers, such as Adobe and Salesforce'.

c3.note: 10-K lists 'Data-focused vendors, such as providers of cloud data warehouses or operational database technologies' as a main competitor category.

c4.note: The data-focused vendor category gives only generic examples (cloud data warehouses, operational databases), no named companies.

c5.note: 10-K says they 'provide data infrastructure but are not purpose-built for consumer data and lack the front-end application layer'.

c6.note: The 10-K passage refers to competitors addressing 'specific aspects of our platform'; the 'established and emerging' wording precedes the excerpt but is consistent.

c7.note: 10-K: 'none of our competitors currently offer comparable solutions that have the comprehensive functionality of our platform'.

c8.note: 10-K says 'We operate in a highly competitive industry'; the FY2024 10-K also calls the market fragmented and highly competitive. The 'evolving' wording is not directly shown but is standard 10-K language.

c9.note: Risk factor: 'We face competition from a number of companies, including Adobe, Salesforce, Mailchimp, and Braze.'

c10.note: The Q3 2026 10-Q repeats the 'Adobe, Salesforce, Mailchimp, and Braze' competition language; the filing mentions Nov 4, 2026 events, so the filing date is consistent.

c11.note: The list is Klaviyo's own self-reported categorization in its 10-K, not a market share ranking.

c13.note: FY2024 10-K contains the same main competitors list and the same risk-factor sentence naming the four companies.

c14.note: Third-party sources add HubSpot, Attentive, Omnisend, Iterable, which the 10-K does not name; Klaviyo's own comparison pages also cover several of them.

c15.note: These firms are cited by third parties as use-case competitors and are absent from the 10-K's named four; Drip is only a third-party listing.

c16.note: Relvino and Klaviyo's own compare pages name most of these rivals; the 10-K names only Adobe, Salesforce, Mailchimp and Braze. Dotdigital is not in the passages.

c17.note: Relvino's Nov 6, 2026 post says this verbatim, including the fifth autonomous decisioning lane.

c18.note: Relvino is itself a competitor selling a rival product. The passages do not show the Mailchimp, Constant Contact or Attentive roundups, but vendor-published lists are plausibly self-interested.

c19.note: The 10-K says competitors could merge or partner with one another or strengthen cooperative relationships with distribution and technology partners; the 'change quickly' part is inference.

c20.note: FY2025 revenue was $1,234.0M, up 31.6% from $937.5M. Newer nine-month 2026 data exists.

c21.note: Stratrix lists Salesforce at $41.5B revenue for the fiscal year to January 2026.

c22.note: Stratrix lists Adobe at $23.8B revenue for the fiscal year to November 2025.

c23.note: Klaviyo's compare page says it has more integrations than Mailchimp, Brevo, Bloomreach, Omnisend and Attentive, and links head-to-head pages against these rivals.

c24.note: The compare page links to a Klaviyo vs Salesforce Marketing Cloud page.

c25.note: HubSpot's comparison page says 'Klaviyo is built for B2C e-commerce marketing.'

c26.note: HubSpot's page says it 'unites your sales and marketing teams, however you go to market.'

c15.note: Klaviyo's Q3 2026 10-Q (period ended Sep 30, 2026) names only Adobe, Salesforce, Mailchimp and Braze as competitors, so Omnisend, Iterable, HubSpot, Attentive and Drip are not on that list. The claim only says they may compete in some areas, which is a fair hedge.
